answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a bond that is slashed when it makes a provably false claim, such as signing conflicting transactions for the same task. A basalt ledger records commitments and evidence, while falcon and sparrow agents independently check disputes; identities with a history of valid work can earn lower bonds, but newcomers cannot. The attacker must therefore lock up capital for every fake identity and risks losing it when fraud is demonstrated, making large-scale impersonation costly rather than merely easy to automate.
